reasons: The cited termination provisions (10.1, 10.2) address only access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and Fee refunds; 16.5 covers only Confidential Information and cross-refers Customer Data elsewhere without creating any return/export or deletion-certification obligation, so no usable transition/data-return clause exists — 'missing' is the correct status and an insert is actionable.

The inserted paragraph is placed in the termination section immediately after 10.2 and tracks the model language on all three material elements: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format, and post-return deletion with written certification. Additions ('or an Order Form', 'make available for extraction', carve-out for routine backups/legal retention consistent with existing 16.5) are proportionate and do not undercut the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, explains what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback. Deterministic checks pass.

Minor, non-disqualifying: the redline does not carry the '10.3' number referenced in the rationale, and the redline conditions the 30-day return on Customer's request while the comment states an unqualified 30 days — cosmetic/consistency points only.
